tagline.text: A giant indoor arena in Bulacan with 55,000 seats that hosted Coldplay

location.label: Location
location.text: Ciudad de Victoria complex, Bocaue and Santa Maria, Bulacan

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Depends on event schedules (the November–May dry season makes travel easier)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Event-based, half a day to 1 day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: From about ₱1,500 (per person, covering transport and meals; tickets are separate for each event)

children.text: The Philippine Arena is an indoor arena with about 55,000 seats in the Ciudad de Victoria complex spanning Bocaue and Santa Maria, Bulacan. Built by the Iglesia ni Cristo, it is a place you visit on the days when concerts, basketball and international tournaments are held.

The Philippine Arena is a large indoor arena about 30 kilometers north of Manila inside Ciudad de Victoria, a tourism development zone spanning Bocaue and Santa Maria in Bulacan. The Iglesia ni Cristo (INC) built it as a project marking the centennial of the church, broke ground on August 17, 2011, completed construction on May 30, 2014, and opened it on July 21 of the same year. The centennial celebration was held on July 27. On that day, Guinness World Records recognized it as the world's largest mixed-use indoor theater.

In scale, the arena seats up to 55,000, with upper and lower bowls of about 25,000 seats each. Behind the stage there is a retractable section of 2,000 seats. The floor measures 220 by 170 meters, the height is about 65 meters, and the oval roof measures 227 by 179 meters. About 9,000 tons of steel were used, and it was designed to withstand earthquake loads. The architecture was handled by the Brisbane, Australia office of Populous, with Hanwha Engineering and Construction as contractor. The design draws inspiration from the narra tree, known as the Philippines' mother tree, and from banyan roots, and the roof recalls the traditional nipa hut. The construction cost differs between sources. Wikipedia gives about US$213 million (about 9.4 billion pesos), while newspaper reports give about 8.7 billion pesos. Construction took about 30 months and two construction workers were reported to have died. Inside, there is a stage level, a main access level, a VIP area with conference rooms and an upper concourse.

This is not a place tourists tour on ordinary days but one you visit when an event is on. It is the home of the Philippine men's national basketball team, and the PBA professional basketball league also plays out-of-town games here. The 2014 PBA opening game drew 52,612 fans, and the January 2023 PBA Finals drew 54,589, setting the PBA attendance record. The 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup held Group A games here and set a World Cup record of 38,115. In concerts, Coldplay drew a combined 96,079 over two nights in January 2024. Blackpink, Bruno Mars, U2, BINI and SB19 have also performed here. Large events beyond sports and music have also been held here, such as the opening ceremony of the 2019 Southeast Asian Games, a political rally in 2022 and the 2023 Asia Artist Awards.

This guide is for travelers heading to a concert or game at the Philippine Arena. On ranking, Wikipedia states that the arena became the world's second-largest indoor arena when the KJC King Dome in Davao opened on September 1, 2026, so it is best to check the latest sources before using the phrase "world's largest." There is no confirmed information about tours of the arena interior or regular public access, so treat the purpose of your visit as attending an event, and confirm schedules and tickets with the official ticketing site.

Two tiers of seating surround the stage like a Greek amphitheater. The seats come in three colors, green, white and red, taken from the Iglesia ni Cristo flag. The viewing angle differs greatly by seating area at events, so check the seating chart when you book. Behind the stage there is a retractable section of about 2,000 seats that is used to suit the type of event.

blocks.title: Architecture inspired by the narra tree and nipa hut

children.text: The roof and exterior are described as inspired by the Philippine narra tree, banyan roots and the nipa hut. The exterior is good for photos around sunset, and some visitors walk the whole complex to admire the architecture.

It is the home arena of the Philippine men's national basketball team and hosts major PBA games. Group A games of the 2023 FIBA World Cup and the 2018 FIBA 3x3 World Cup were also held here. It is the place where you can feel the passion of Filipino basketball fans most strongly.

Coldplay drew 96,079 over two nights in January 2024, and Blackpink, Bruno Mars and U2 are also reported to have performed here. Some years include stops on K-pop artists' world tours, so check concert news.

The opening ceremony of the 2019 Southeast Asian Games (SEA Games), the TV special "Sa Tamang Panahon" on October 24, 2015 (an attendance of 55,000) and the 2023 Asia Artist Awards were held here. It is also used as a stage for national and broadcast events.

blocks.title: Next to the Philippine Sports Stadium

children.text: Right next door is the INC-owned Philippine Sports Stadium, which hosts field and athletics events. The arena cannot host field events because of its size. Depending on the event, you may go to either facility, so check the venue printed on your ticket.

The complex that contains the arena is described as a tourism and development zone of about 140 hectares. Facilities such as the Eraño Manalo Medical Center and the New Era University Bulacan campus are inside the complex. Four large facilities are reported in the complex, including the Philippine Sports Stadium and the Philippine Sports Center.

The arena itself is indoors, so the weather matters little, but the travel stretches are affected. The November–May dry season keeps the roads dry and travel easy. On event days the roads around the arena get congested early, so you need to plan to arrive well before the start time.

Events are held throughout the year, and big concerts are often in the dry season, such as January–February or November. The schedule differs every year, so confirm it with the official ticketing site.

Between 2022 and 2024, a political rally, the World Cup and big concerts followed one another and the complex was very crowded. On such days the roads back up for several kilometers, so allow twice your usual travel time.

Around the arena, temporary stalls and food trucks appear during events, and it is quiet at other times. In Bocaue and Santa Maria towns there are local restaurants and fast-food outlets where you can eat before or after events. Food inside the venue is pricey and the lines are long, so many visitors eat before they go in. There are few large shopping malls around the complex, so buy what you need in Manila beforehand.

Hotels nearby fill up early for big events, so you can stay in central Manila or Quezon City and travel by chartered vehicle, or book a place in Bulacan or Pampanga in advance. If your way home is not settled, always move with your group for safety.
Buy tickets only from the official ticketing site and avoid resold scalper tickets.
Arrive at least 4 hours before the start and decide on your way home in advance. Allow time for finding your seat and the security check queue.
Prohibited items and bag sizes differ by event, so check the announcement.
After an event, deliberately waiting about an hour before leaving helps you avoid the crush.
Bring your phone battery, cash and ID.
The air-conditioning inside the arena is strong, so bring a light jacket.
For outdoor travel, bring a hat, water and an umbrella.
Cash may be needed around the venue, so prepare some small bills.
Your entry gate is printed on your ticket, so check your seating area and gate number in advance.
On event days the roads around Bocaue are extremely congested and transport home is short, so decide how you will return in advance.
On days without events, interior tours are not confirmed, so ask in advance so you do not make a wasted trip.
Scalpers and fake-ticket scams exist, so buy only through official channels.
In crowded places, keep your belongings and phone close to your body.
Stops and fares change from time to time, so check the latest announcements.
